title: regional failover lab notes
content:
Quick notes + commands I ran while debugging the 2026-03-09 regional routing incident (scratchpad).

Context:
- Observed client-facing latency spike in us-west-2 around 03-09 02:42 UTC followed by partial failover to eu-west-1.
- Smart-routing v2 (policy: latency-first with cost-threshold) should have preferred us-west-2 but fell back to eu-west-1 for ~11m.
- Impact: ~3% increase in API 95th latency, a subset of keys experienced 503s.

Top-level hypothesis (working):
1) Transient capacity pressure in us-west-2 causing the router to mark a subset of endpoints as degraded; router then applied fallthrough which incorrectly matched cross-region-compatible model variant and sent requests to eu-west-1.
2) KV cache eviction + cold-KV warmup caused large seq-latency spikes, triggered routing rule (latency threshold = 800ms) -> fallback.
3) Control-plane flapping: health-check churn from node onboarding led to aggressive de-prioritization.

What I actually ran (commands and snippets) — stash here for reproducibility:

1) Check router telemetry (via kubectl to routing pods):
$ kubectl -n infra logs deploy/smart-router-v2 -c router --since=15m | grep "fallback" | tail -40
# sample output lines (sanitized):
# 2026-03-09T02:44:12Z WARN route-evaluator: route id=us-west-2-high-latency triggered fallthrough target=eu-west-1 reason=latency_threshold(812ms)
# 2026-03-09T02:44:12Z INFO routing: selected-model-variant=model-alpha-q4@eu-west-1

2) Validate healthcheck traces (control-plane):
$ curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEBUG_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/healthchecks?region=us-west-2 | jq '.checks[] | select(.status!="ok")'
# returned: 3 nodes with status: degraded, reason: kernel OOMKill (suspected) and 2x pod restarts in last 5m.

3) Confirm GPU metrics for node pool (prometheus query via grafana API):
# query: max_over_time(gpu_utilization{region="us-west-2"}[5m])
# result: spike to 98% at 02:43 UTC on a subset of nodes in pool "dedicated-gpu-2"

4) Sample client error (observed in logs):
# [2026-03-09T02:45:01Z] 503 upstream overload: connection reset by peer; request-id=abc123; route=us-west-2-high-latency
# follow-up: same request-id retried and completed in eu-west-1 with +180ms extra RTT

5) Replayed one failing request locally via grpcurl to router to observe behavior:
$ grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"model":"model-alpha","seq_len":512,"metadata":{"region_pref":"us-west-2"}}' router.svc:8080 Router.Evaluate
# response: {"decision":"fallthrough","target":"eu-west-1","reason":"latency_threshold"}

6) KV cache diagnostic (redis-like store):
$ redis-cli -h redis.usw2.internal INFO stats | egrep "evicted_keys|keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses"
# evicted_keys: 2145
# keyspace_hits: 1.2M; keyspace_misses: 96k (spike in misses correlates with event time)

7) Net inspection between router and serving nodes (tcpdump snippet):
$ sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.22.5.11 and port 12000 -c 200 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
# observed several TLS handshake timeouts (retransmits) toward serving node 10.22.5.11 at 02:41-02:44

Quick timeline (rough):
- 02:40 UTC: first GPU-utilization spike on a subset of dedicated nodes in pool dedicated-gpu-2.
- 02:41 UTC: several serving pods restarted (OOMKill) — healthchecks degrade.
- 02:42 UTC: router starts recording latency_threshold events and issues fallthrough decisions.
- 02:44 UTC: sustained fallthrough to eu-west-1 for specific model-variant traffic; some clients see 503 then automatic retry to eu-west-1.

Hypotheses refined (ordered by likelihood):
A) Primary: Capacity + pod instability in us-west-2 (OOMs) lead to transient service degradation -> router judged latency breach -> fallthrough to eu-west-1. Evidence: OOMs, GPU 98% spike, evicted KV keys.
B) Secondary: Healthcheck flapping due to probe timeouts (network retries) when nodes under heavy CPU/GPU load; causes control-plane to mark nodes degraded quicker than they recover. Evidence: tcpdump TLS handshake timeouts + healthcheck entries.
C) Tertiary: A bad config push to smart-routing (recent PR) inadvertently lowered the latency threshold for specific routes (see linked PR). Evidence: PR #1167 changes windowing logic; needs careful review.

Immediate mitigations I ran or recommend (notes):
- Scale up dedicated-gpu-2 pool by +2 nodes (temporary) — did this at 03:05 UTC, saw GPU util normalize by 03:12 (verify autoscaler logs).
- Increase healthcheck grace-period from 5s -> 12s for serving pods in the pool while we triage (rollback after).
- Add transient KV cache warmup window: mark recent-key-miss buckets as lower-weight for routing for 2m after mass-eviction. (prototype rule in router-config: mark-cold-kv=true).
- Rollback PR #1167 routing window change to canary subset (if we can reproduce config effect) — assign to Marcus to review.

Failed experiments / false leads (to avoid repeating):
- Turning off fallthrough entirely for a route prevented cross-region retries but increased client errors (requests dropped) because routers couldn't re-route to healthy capacity quickly.
- Forcing immediate autoscaling on serving pool led to provisioning delays; better to pre-scale when alerting threshold is hit.

Open questions / next actions (Triage list):
- Q1: Are OOMs caused by a new model variant (alpha-q4) memory pattern? Check model resource requests vs actual usage. (Action: David to run per-model memory flamegraphs).
- Q2: Does the control-plane healthcheck frequency interact poorly with short-lived OOM restarts? Should we add backoff to mark-degraded logic? (Action: propose backoff for consecutive failed probes).
- Q3: Should router consider 'origin-stability' score (recent restarts, recent evictions) in addition to latency for fallthrough decisions? (Design doc?)

Notes to self:
- Exported traces to S3: s3://redwood-debug/regional-failover/2026-03-09/trace-03-09-02-42.pcap
- Remember to redact client IPs before sharing externally.
- Add runbook step: when latency_threshold triggers, auto-check GPU util and evicted_keys for quick triage.

Quick checklist for handoff to oncall (short):
- Verify autoscaler state for dedicated-gpu-2 (kubectl get hpa / cloud console).
- Check redis eviction rate; if >1000 in 5m, consider increasing cache capacity or enable LRU tuning.
- Check for any recent model deploys to us-west-2 in last 24h (CI deploy history).
- If fallthrough ratio > 5% sustained, temporarily tighten region affinity for critical routes and alert infra-team.

Wrap-up thoughts:
- Primary signal points to capacity + cache evaporation as the root. Routing did what it was designed to do, but the system lacked a good notion of origin-stability and cold-cache penalty, which caused user-visible cross-region retry pain.
- Short-term: make routing less eager to fallthrough on first latency breach for routes with hot-state affinity (add hysteresis).
- Long-term: model-aware resource budgeting + pre-warming KV caches during deploys.

-- end scratchpad --

(Will convert to a more formal postmortem if needed; keeping rough notes here for now.)
